direction_03.design: Montserrat 900 headings, an asymmetric material photograph, an editorial service list with square thumbnails, capability rows and a different project sequence. Its utility bar is removed and an eight-service navigation row sits below the header.
direction_03.prompt: Photorealistic editorial industrial product photograph, landscape 3:2 composition, for a bespoke British sheet-metal fabricator website. Sculptural arrangement of four accurately folded long aluminium and galvanised steel flashing profiles on a lightly worn charcoal workbench. Strong crisp 90-degree folded edges, varied L and Z section profiles, detailed satin metal texture. Tight three-quarter close view with some diagonal profiles leading from foreground left to upper right, meaningful material scale and real fabrication detail. Background is a modest clean workshop in soft focus, no people, no logos, no text. Palette silver, deep navy blue and charcoal, natural daylight, tactile honest materials, contemporary architectural magazine photograph, understated precision rather than glossy futuristic factory. Leave the right fifth with dark subtle workshop detail so image can crop, primary metal detail dominates center-left. No sparks, robots, giant multinational factory, melted metal, fake lettering or dramatic orange lighting. This is illustrative photography direction, not a claimed depiction of any real premises.

existing_assets: dist/assets/logo.png and the product/project JPEGs derive from the existing company website. Project originals and usage rights should be confirmed before a public launch.

generated_asset.purpose: Illustrative workshop photography direction, explicitly labelled in both concepts. Does not depict FFS premises, staff or machinery.
generated_asset.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create one high-resolution 3:2 landscape editorial photograph for a British sheet-metal fabricator website concept. It is illustrative, not a depiction of a specific real business. An authentic, tidy small-to-medium industrial workshop in West Sussex, England. Foreground crisp long folded silver metal flashing profiles on a sturdy workbench, rich tactile brushed zinc and aluminium surfaces, angular folds catching soft natural side light. Behind them a substantial press brake and a single adult fabricator wearing proper safety eyewear and dark blue workwear, slightly out of focus, normal human scale. Muted navy machinery, natural concrete grey, a subtle restrained burgundy detail. Daylight through factory windows, honest working atmosphere, modern premium documentary photography. Composition: profiles lead from lower left towards mid-right, machine and worker deeper in frame, shallow depth of field but credible workshop detail. No sparks, no dramatic molten metal, no welding, no futuristic robots, no cavernous multinational factory, no hard hat indoors without need, no signage, no text, no logos. This should communicate precise workmanship and an approachable local company.
